documents.IDD-0201.spec-editor.md:
# Editor
Users edit one local plaintext note. Syntax highlighting and search are basic and bounded; local persistence is explicitly disabled. There are no external integrations. Input is sequential. The only confirmed error case is an invalid keyboard shortcut.
documents.IDD-0202.spec-input.md:
# Input
The editor supports one documented unusual shortcut conflict: Escape closes the dialog, except while a key binding capture is running, when Escape cancels capture.

expected: Do not use feature inventory or a broad High label as a substitute for source-grounded causality for each dimension.
Independently justify any High, including whether the shortcut exception alone warrants it; do not inflate Data Complexity or Integrations.

scenarios.request: Evaluate every dimension without artificially reducing a genuine High classification.

documents.IDD-0201.spec-network-console.md:
# Distributed operations console
The product spans approvals, offline scheduling, audit reporting, emergency rollback and two actor roles. Every approval changes an immutable cross-region ledger, with conflict-free replay after partitions, strict monotonic sequencing and simultaneous edits. It merges four vendor streams with independent retry protocols, idempotent actions and compensations. A live terminal dashboard supports keyboard/mouse interaction while streams repaint and modals resize. It must operate under hard 50 ms screen refresh deadlines, work disconnected and enforce role-separated authorization and verifiable recovery.
documents.IDD-0202.spec-contracts.md:
# Accepted constraints
Rollback must never erase an approved audit record; once connectivity resumes, reconciled state must preserve actor-specific authorization and externally confirmed actions.

expected: Allow High for all seven dimensions if independently justified by concrete requirements, not simply because another dimension is High.
Explain distinct mechanisms for scope, rules, integration contracts, ledger data consistency, security/recovery, live interaction and operational deadlines.

scenarios.request: Assess complexity of integrations separately from stored data.

documents.IDD-0301.spec-providers.md:
# Providers
Files can be browsed via local disk, FTP, FTPS and SFTP. Each remote provider has different authentication, listing, cancellation and failure behavior. The panel retries unavailable providers without freezing the other panel.
documents.IDD-0302.spec-data.md:
# Data
Each panel holds only a current path and transient file names and sizes. No persistent database, versioning, metadata migration or cross-provider data model is required.

expected: Recognize meaningful provider contracts and failure behavior in Integrations, but do not transfer that rating into Data Complexity.
Use the explicit simple state/lifecycle to distinguish Data Complexity and justify each dimension separately.

scenarios.request: Assess this single-feature tool.

documents.IDD-0401.spec-solver.md:
# Route solver
The single user action optimizes routes for 800 vehicles with precedence, exclusivity, variable traffic and deadline constraints. It must find the global minimum expected penalty, not a simple greedy approximation.

expected: Permit Small Product Scope and High Implementation Complexity based on the globally constrained algorithm.
Explain that the number of actions or source documents is not a proxy for difficulty.

scenarios.request: Assess the whole product and identify the most consequential confirmed drivers.

documents.IDD-0501.spec-copy.md:
# Copy
Users perform resumable file transfers. On partial failures, restart must verify block checksums and must never corrupt an existing target.
documents.IDD-0502.spec-ui.md:
# Terminal UI
Input is routed through nested modal dialogs while live progress updates and screen resizing occur; restoring focus cannot drop a queued user command.
documents.IDD-0503.spec-export.md:
# Export
Users export recent transfer activity to CSV with a header.
documents.IDD-0504.spec-sftp.md:
# Remote connection
SFTP connections can disconnect mid-transfer, and authentication failures must be surfaced for safe retry.

expected: Top Complexity Drivers rank supported recovery, interactive concurrency and remote failures above trivial CSV export, explaining why, without numeric points.
For each main driver cite source, affected area and relevant dimensions, while retaining the separate area map.

scenarios.request: Assess cross-area behavior without multiplying product scope.

documents.IDD-0602.spec-payment.md:
